# Polska: Poland as a strategy map built from real data: full text

Every atlas page of https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/ as compact markdown. Generated 2026-11-26. Each figure gives its date and publisher.

## Poland in numbers

Poland had 37,332,510 residents on 31 December 2025, 2.9% fewer than in 2015.

The country has 16 voivodeships, 2,479 gminas, 380 powiats and 1,026 towns.

Its GDP was 3.92 trillion zł in 2025. Mazowieckie, around Warszawa, is the largest voivodeship by population and produced 23.9% of the national GDP in 2024.

Each voivodeship and each town of 20,000 or more people has its own page below, with its figures and their sources.

### National figures

- Population: 37,332,510 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -2.9% (from 38,434,668) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 3.92 trillion zł (2025; Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- GDP per resident: 104,879 zł (2025 GDP, 2025 residents; Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 9,178 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 5.8% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 15,125,030 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,328 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- UNESCO World Heritage properties: 18 (2026; UNESCO World Heritage Centre (data.unesco.org); Narodowy Instytut Dziedzictwa (dane.gov.pl))
- National parks: 23 (2024; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); Wikidata)
- Visits to national parks: 16,390,532 (2024; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); Wikidata)

## Dolnośląskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/dolnoslaskie/

Dolnośląskie has the 2nd highest average gross wage of the 16 voivodeships: 9,208 zł a month in May 2026.

Its capital is Wrocław.

It has 93 towns; 16 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 2,857,273 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -1.6% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 302 billion zł (8.3% of Poland) (2024; Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 9,208 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 5.5% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 1,117,241 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,593 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 82.1 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 75.2 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 4.4 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 6.7 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 41% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Wrocław](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wroclaw/): 672,601 residents
- [Wałbrzych](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/walbrzych/): 97,546 residents
- [Legnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/legnica/): 89,919 residents
- [Jelenia Góra](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/jelenia-gora/): 73,470 residents
- [Lubin](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/lubin/): 65,961 residents
- [Głogów](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/glogow/): 60,605 residents
- [Świdnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/swidnica/): 51,357 residents
- [Bolesławiec](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/boleslawiec/): 36,642 residents
- [Oleśnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/olesnica/): 34,676 residents
- [Oława](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/olawa/): 32,928 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Churches of Peace in Jawor and Świdnica: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2001
- Centennial Hall in Wrocław: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2006
- Karkonoski Park Narodowy: National park, 2,400,000 visits in 2024
- Park Narodowy Gór Stołowych: National park, 1,296,300 visits in 2024
- Uniwersytet Wrocławski: University, 21,426 students on 31 December 2025

### Energy and resources

- Elektrownia Turów: Lignite power plant, 1,995 MW
- Elektrociepłownia Wrocław: Hard-coal power plant, 260 MW
- Elektrociepłownia Czechnica 2: Gas power plant, 179 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna PV Kotla: Solar power plant, 130 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna PV Miłkowice: Solar power plant, 113 MW
- Farma fotowoltaiczna Proszówek: Solar power plant, 55 MW
- KWB Turów: Lignite mine, 7.0 Mt lignite (2025)
- Głogów Głęboki-Przemysłowy (shaft GG-1): Copper mine
- ZG Lubin: Copper mine
- ZG Polkowice-Sieroszowice: Copper mine
- ZG Rudna: Copper mine
- Huta Miedzi Cedynia: Copper smelter

## Kujawsko-Pomorskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/kujawsko-pomorskie/

Kujawsko-Pomorskie has the least tree cover of the 16 voivodeships: 31% of its land.

The voivode sits in Bydgoszcz and the regional assembly (sejmik) in Toruń.

It has 56 towns; 7 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 1,971,891 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: -5.5% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 154 billion zł (4.2% of Poland) (2024; Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 8,206 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 7.7% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 660,444 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 3,845 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 81.7 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 74.7 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 2.5 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 4.1 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 31% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Bydgoszcz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/bydgoszcz/): 321,100 residents
- [Toruń](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/torun/): 192,784 residents
- [Włocławek](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wloclawek/): 98,038 residents
- [Grudziądz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/grudziadz/): 86,811 residents
- [Inowrocław](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/inowroclaw/): 65,742 residents
- [Brodnica](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/brodnica/): 27,695 residents
- [Świecie](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/swiecie/): 24,472 residents
- Chełmno: 17,540 residents
- Nakło nad Notecią: 16,638 residents
- Rypin: 15,143 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Medieval Town of Toruń: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1997

### Energy and resources

- Budowa bloku gazowo-parowego CCGT w Grudziądzu: Gas power plant, 560 MW (under_construction)
- Elektrociepłownia Gazowo-Parowa Anwil Włocławek: Gas power plant, 463 MW
- PGE Energia Ciepła S.A. Oddział Elektrociepłownia w Bydgoszczy: Hard-coal power plant, 187 MW

- Life expectancy at birth, men: 74.2 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

- Life expectancy at birth, men: 73.9 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

## Małopolskie

Voivodeship of Poland. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/malopolskie/

Małopolskie has the 2nd most tourist nights per resident of the 16 voivodeships: 5.0 in 2025.

Its capital is Kraków.

It has 64 towns; 12 of them have 20,000 or more residents.

### Figures

- Population: 3,429,342 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Change since 2015: +1.7% (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- GDP: 297 billion zł (8.1% of Poland) (2024; Eurostat and European Central Bank)
- Average gross wage: 9,119 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 5.0% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working: 1,406,960 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue of the gminas per resident: 4,269 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, women: 83.6 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Life expectancy at birth, men: 76.8 years (2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tourist nights per resident: 5.0 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- New dwellings per 1,000 residents: 5.9 (2025; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Tree cover: 55% of the land (2021; European Space Agency (ESA WorldCover consortium))

### Largest towns

- [Kraków](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/krakow/): 816,614 residents
- [Tarnów](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/tarnow/): 101,177 residents
- [Nowy Sącz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/nowy-sacz/): 79,416 residents
- [Oświęcim](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/oswiecim/): 35,005 residents
- [Chrzanów](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/chrzanow/): 33,193 residents
- [Nowy Targ](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/nowy-targ/): 32,956 residents
- [Olkusz](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/olkusz/): 31,538 residents
- [Wieliczka](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/wieliczka/): 28,485 residents
- [Bochnia](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/bochnia/): 28,187 residents
- [Zakopane](https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/zakopane/): 24,921 residents

### Heritage, parks and landmarks

- Historic Centre of Kraków: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1978
- Wieliczka and Bochnia Royal Salt Mines: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1978
- Auschwitz Birkenau German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp (1940-1945): Memorial and museum, UNESCO World Heritage since 1979
- Kalwaria Zebrzydowska: the Mannerist Architectural and Park Landscape Complex and Pilgrimage Park: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1999
- Wooden Churches of Southern Małopolska: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2003
- Wooden Tserkvas of the Carpathian Region in Poland and Ukraine: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2013
- Tatrzański Park Narodowy: National park, 5,091,772 visits in 2024
- Pieniński Park Narodowy: National park, 1,180,600 visits in 2024
- Uniwersytet Jagielloński w Krakowie: University, 33,369 students on 31 December 2025

### Energy and resources

- PGE Energia Ciepła Oddział nr 1 w Krakowie: Hard-coal power plant, 460 MW
- ResInvest Energy Skawina S.A.: Hard-coal power plant, 330 MW
- Elektrownia Siersza: Hard-coal power plant, 306 MW
- Rzezawa 60: Solar power plant, 60 MW
- ZG Janina: Hard-coal mine
- Kopalnia Soli Bochnia: Salt mine (historic)
- Kopalnia Soli Wieliczka: Salt mine (historic)

## Warszawa

Warszawa, Mazowieckie. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/warszawa/

Warszawa is the capital and the largest town of Poland, with 1,866,729 residents on 31 December 2025.

Warszawa is the capital of Poland and a city with powiat rights in Mazowieckie voivodeship. It is the capital of Mazowieckie.

### Figures

- Population: 1,866,729 (31 December 2025; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: +7.0% (from 1,744,351) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 42.2 years (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 20.2% (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage: 12,059 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 1.6% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 8,040 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- University students per 1,000 residents: 140 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working in the city: 1,983,029 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

City type: Capital city. Capital of Poland.

Jobs by employer seat on 31 December 2025, against the share of each kind of work in Poland.

- Commercial hub district (Trade, Finance, Real estate, Business services): 637,049 workers, 1.5 times the national share; Finance alone 4.0 times
- Campus district (IT & telecoms, Science & engineering, Schools & universities): 522,772 workers, 1.5 times the national share; IT & telecoms alone 2.6 times
- Theater square district (Arts, sport & recreation): 31,746 workers, 1.4 times the national share

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 68.2% of valid votes in Warszawa and Karol Nawrocki 31.8%. Turnout was 83.2%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

### Air quality

PM2.5 averaged 15.6 µg/m³ in 2025 at the GIOŚ station Warszawa, al. Niepodległości (3 km).

The median of the 154 towns of 20,000+ with a station within 25 km was 16.4 µg/m³.

### Metro area and places nearby

Warszawa belongs to the Warszawa metro area, 3,535,827 residents in 97 gminas.

- Uniwersytet Warszawski: University, 39,852 students on 31 December 2025, in the town
- Politechnika Warszawska: University, 20,953 students on 31 December 2025, in the town
- Varso Tower: Tallest building in Poland: 310 m (2022), in the town
- Historic Centre of Warsaw: UNESCO World Heritage site since 1980, 2 km away
- Warszawa-Chopin: Busiest airport by passengers: 24,079,757 passengers (2025), 8 km away

### Towns of a similar size

Katowice has 187 university students per 1,000 residents, the 4th highest share of the 84 towns of 20,000+ with a university.

Katowice is a city with powiat rights in Śląskie voivodeship. It is the capital of Śląskie.

### Figures

- Population: 277,415 (31 December 2025; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: -7.5% (from 299,910) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 45.0 years (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 24.1% (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage: 10,112 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment: 1.9% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 6,272 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))
- University students per 1,000 residents: 187 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- People working in the city: 255,529 (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

City type: Coal town. KWK Staszic-Wujek.

Jobs by employer seat on 31 December 2025, against the share of each kind of work in Poland.

- Mining (Industrial zone district): 36,115 workers, 17.3 times the national share
- Government plaza district (Public administration & defence): 32,984 workers, 1.8 times the national share
- Theater square district (Arts, sport & recreation): 3,820 workers, 1.3 times the national share

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 63.1% of valid votes in Katowice and Karol Nawrocki 36.9%. Turnout was 74.8%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

### Air quality

PM2.5 averaged 18.1 µg/m³ in 2025 at the GIOŚ station Katowice, ul. Dudy-Gracza (6 km).

The median of the 154 towns of 20,000+ with a station within 25 km was 16.4 µg/m³.

### Metro area and places nearby

Katowice belongs to the Górnośląsko-Zagłębiowska metro area (PL010F, PL055F, PL061F, PL070F), 2,021,558 residents in 39 gminas.

- Tarnowskie Góry Lead-Silver-Zinc Mine and its Underground Water Management System: UNESCO World Heritage site since 2017, 24 km away
- Auschwitz Birkenau German Nazi Concentration and Extermination Camp (1940-1945): Memorial and museum, UNESCO World Heritage since 1979, 29 km away

Ostrów Wielkopolski had 68,111 residents on 31 December 2025, 6.2% fewer than in 2015.

Ostrów Wielkopolski is a town in powiat ostrowski, Wielkopolskie voivodeship.

### Figures

- Population: 68,111 (31 December 2025; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: -6.2% (from 72,635) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 46.2 years (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 24.3% (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage (powiat ostrowski): 7,544 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment (powiat ostrowski): 4.3% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 4,052 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

These figures describe the jobs in powiat ostrowski, by employer seat, on 31 December 2025.

- Industrial zone district (Mining, Manufacturing): 19,143 workers, 1.7 times the national share

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 61.2% of valid votes in Ostrów Wielkopolski and Karol Nawrocki 38.8%. Turnout was 72.0%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

## Mrągowo

Mrągowo, powiat mrągowski, Warmińsko-Mazurskie. Page: https://softonsofa.com/pol-civ/atlas/mragowo/

The average gross wage around Mrągowo (powiat mrągowski) was 7,238 zł a month in May 2026, the 6th lowest for any of the 204 Polish towns with 20,000 or more people.

Mrągowo is a town in powiat mrągowski, Warmińsko-Mazurskie voivodeship.

### Figures

- Population: 20,008 (31 December 2025; Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS); OpenStreetMap contributors)
- Change since 2015: -9.1% (from 22,005) (2015 to 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Median age: 46.1 years (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Residents aged 65 or more: 23.6% (31 December 2025; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Average gross wage (powiat mrągowski): 7,238 zł a month (May 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Registered unemployment (powiat mrągowski): 10.1% (October 2026; Statistics Poland (GUS))
- Personal income tax revenue per resident: 3,608 zł (2026 plan; Ministry of Finance and Statistics Poland (GUS))

### City type and districts

City type: Tourist town. Hotels and restaurants: 2.8 times the national share of workers.

These figures describe the jobs in powiat mrągowski, by employer seat, on 31 December 2025.

- Entertainment complex district (Hotels & restaurants): 779 workers, 2.8 times the national share

### 2025 presidential election

In the presidential runoff of 1 June 2025, Rafał Trzaskowski won 56.1% of valid votes in Mrągowo and Karol Nawrocki 43.9%. Turnout was 67.0%.

In the Sejm election of 15 October 2023 the largest committee there was Koalicja Obywatelska.

### Air quality

No GIOŚ station measured PM2.5 within 25 km of the town centre in 2025.
